A label with which TestCase::classify() classified examples of a property, with the number of examples that were classified with it.

An example that falsified a property: the choices from which its arguments were generated, its arguments, the values that it drew, and the steps of its state machine, exported as PHP code, or the explicit example that falsified the property.
A value that an example of a property drew with draw(), exported as PHP code, with the label that was passed to draw().
A label with which TestCase::observe() observed numeric values of examples of a property, with the number of values that were observed with it and their statistics.
Another way in which a property was falsified while its counterexample was shrunk, with the simplest counterexample that falsified it that way.
A label with which TestCase::target() targeted scores for examples of a property, with the highest score that an example reached.
An emitter that collects the events emitted through it into an event collection that can later be flushed and replayed, without disturbing the global event facade.

The collection window a dispatcher opens to divert events: between startCollectingEvents() and stopCollectingEvents(), dispatched events are collected instead of being processed, so that the window's owner — a RetryTestSuite suppressing the events of a failed attempt, for example — decides what becomes of them.

A destination for events that can divert them: between startCollectingEvents() and stopCollectingEvents(), the events emitted into it are handed back to the caller instead of being processed, and the caller decides with forward() which of them become part of the test run's event stream after all.

Specifies a public static method of the test class that describes the counterexample of a property: when the property is falsified, the method is called with the arguments of the counterexample, and the string that it returns is reported below these arguments, which are reported as PHP code.

Specifies a public static method of a class that describes the counterexample of a property: when the property is falsified, the method is called with the arguments of the counterexample, and the string that it returns is reported below these arguments, which are reported as PHP code.

Specifies the generator for a parameter of a property: either the name of a public static method of the test case class that returns the generator, or a static closure that returns it. A public static method of another class is specified with #[ForAllExternal].

Specifies the generator for a parameter of a property with a public static method of another class than the test case class that returns it, for instance #[ForAllExternal(MoneyGenerators::class, 'smallAmounts')].

A parameter of a rule or of a method with #[InitializeStateMachine] of a state machine with this attribute receives one of the values that earlier steps added to the pool, rather than a generated value. With $consume, the value is removed from the pool.

Registers a public static method of a test case class that returns a generator as the generator for every value of exactly the given class that a property of the test case class needs, including the values that are needed to create objects of other classes with new.

A public method of a state machine with this attribute is called once before TestCase::runStateMachine() takes the steps of the state machine, with generated values or values that earlier methods with this attribute produced (#[FromPool]) as its arguments. The value that it returns is added to the pool that is named with $produces. The methods with this attribute that a parent class declares are called before those of the class that extends it.

A method with this attribute is a property: a test method whose parameters receive generated values. The property is checked for the given number of examples, or the configured default number of examples when it is null.

Requires that at least the given percentage of the examples of a property that are checked are classified with the given label by TestCase::classify(). A property for which this is not the case is considered risky.

A public method of a state machine with this attribute is an invariant: TestCase::runStateMachine() calls it after the methods with

[InitializeStateMachine] and after every step, or, with $atEnd, only after

the methods with #[InitializeStateMachine] and after the last step, which is meant for invariants that are expensive to check. An invariant does not hold when it fails an assertion or raises an exception.

A public method of a state machine with this attribute is a rule: a step that TestCase::runStateMachine() can take. Its parameters receive generated values, or values that earlier steps produced (#[FromPool]). The rule is only taken while the public method of the state machine that is named as its precondition returns true. The value that the rule returns is added to the pool that is named with $produces.

Uses the generators that the public static methods of the given class register with #[GeneratorFor] for the properties of a test case class, or for one property. A generator that the test case class registers takes precedence over one that a class used for the property registers, which takes precedence over one that a class used for the test case class registers.
Base class for all PHPUnit Framework exceptions.
Exception for expectations which failed their check.
A test suite that aggregates the executions of a single test method, such as the repetitions of a repeated test or the attempts of a retried test.
Records, in the order in which they happen, the invocations of methods of mock objects that were registered using MockObject::recordInvocationsIn().

A test suite that aggregates the repetitions or attempts of a single PHPT test. Unlike the repetitions and attempts of a test method, a PHPT test does not track its own status, so the outcome of each run is determined from the events it emits.

Reports that an object of a class, for which a generator was derived from the types of the parameters of its constructor, cannot be created because the constructor does not accept the arguments that were generated for it: the constructor of a value object that validates its arguments, for instance.
Thrown when no generator can be derived from a type. The message names the parameter and the type that could not be handled.
Provides the choices from which generators build the arguments of an example, and records them as the example's choice sequence.

The objects that generators created with new while an example was generated, together with the arguments that were passed to their constructors. An object is exported as the expression that created it, even when its state was changed afterwards.
Exports the arguments of a counterexample as PHP expressions that can be copied into a data provider for a regression test.

Derives generators from the types of parameters: from the type in the parameter's @param tag (including @phpstan-param and @psalm-param) if there is one, from the type in the @var tag (including @phpstan-var and @psalm-var) of the doc comment of a promoted constructor parameter that has no @param tag, and from its native type declaration otherwise. The tags are read from the source file when OPcache has discarded the doc comments.
The generators that a test case class registers with #[GeneratorFor] for classes. Such a generator is used for every value of exactly that class.

Draws the values that the body of an example of a property draws with TestCase::draw(), and the steps of the state machine that it runs with TestCase::runStateMachine(), from the choice source that generated its arguments, so that they are replayed and shrunk together with the arguments.
Aggregates the events of the examples of a property, which are collected rather than dispatched, into the events that are reported for the property.
Thrown by TestCase::assume(), and by TestCase::draw() when no value can be generated, to discard the current example of a property.
Thrown while the arguments for an example are generated when the example has to be discarded, for instance because a filter could not be satisfied.

The result of an example of a property that was run on its own rather than while the property was checked: whether it passed, was rejected, skipped, or marked as incomplete, falsified the property, or was aborted without checking the property, and the choices from which its arguments and the values that it drew were generated.

Builds and runs the examples of a property: it creates the test case of an example, generates its arguments from a source of choices, runs it with its events collected, handles the issues that are triggered while values are generated as issues of the property, and exports arguments as PHP code.

An example of a property whose arguments are specified with #[TestWith] or

[TestWithJson] instead of being generated.
How an example falsified a property.
How a property was falsified, as it is reported: with the Test\PropertyFalsified event and as part of the failure or error of the property.

Reports how a property was falsified: by an explicit example, whose failure or error is reported as it is, or by a generated example, which is replayed to tell whether it falsifies the property again, whose counterexample is shrunk, and whose minimal counterexample is replayed, as are the simplest counterexamples of the other ways in which the property was falsified while it was shrunk.
Tells which of the issues that an example triggered falsify its property.
Reports a property that was falsified by an example, but not when that example was replayed, or not when its minimal counterexample was replayed.

A public static method that returns a generator: a method that is registered with #[GeneratorFor], or one that is specified with #[ForAll] or

[ForAllExternal].

Validates the classes and the methods with which generators are created: the generator that is specified with #[ForAll] or #[ForAllExternal] for a parameter, the classes that are used with #[UseGenerators], and the methods that are registered with #[GeneratorFor].
Reports a generator that refers to itself before it makes a choice, so that generating a value with it would recurse infinitely.

Resolves the generators of the parameters of a property from its definition: the generators that were derived from the types of the parameters, the generator methods and closures that are specified with

[ForAll], and the generators that are registered for classes.
A generator builds a value from the choices it draws from a choice source.
Generates arrays with keys and values of the given generators. A key that is already present in the array is not added again.
Generates false (choice 0) and true (choice 1).
Generates arbitrary binary strings. Each byte is one choice, its value.

The code points of the characters that a string generator chooses from, given as ranges. The ranges are sorted, ranges that overlap or adjoin each other are merged, and surrogates, which are not characters, are left out.
Generates the same value without drawing a choice.
Generates points in time from a minimum to a maximum, in one of the time zones, as DateTimeImmutable objects.

A generator that is derived from a type only when it generates its first value, by the deriver of the choice source. This way, the generators that the test case class of the property registers for types are used, even for the generators that are created while an example is generated.
Generates domain names of letters, digits, and hyphens (RFC 1123) in lowercase, without a trailing dot.
Generates one of the given values. The choice is the index of the value, so the first value is the simplest one.
Generates email addresses (RFC 5321) of at most 254 characters, with a local part of at most 64 characters.
Generates values of the given generator until one satisfies the predicate.
Generates a value of the given generator, and then a value of the generator that the mapper returns for it.
Generates floating-point numbers from three choices: the sign (0 for positive), whether the magnitude is an integer (0) or not (1), and the magnitude.
Generates integers in the range [$minimum, $maximum]. The choice 0 stands for the value closest to zero.
Generates IPv4 addresses of a network in dotted decimal notation.

Generates IPv6 addresses of a network in the canonical text representation of RFC 5952: lowercase hexadecimal digits without leading zeros, the first longest run of at least two groups of zeros compressed to "::", and the last 32 bits of an IPv4-mapped address in dotted decimal notation.
Generates lists of the values of a generator. In a list of unique elements, no element equals another one: an element that does is generated again.
Generates null (choice 0) or a value of the given generator (choice 1).

Generates objects of a class with new, using an argument of the respective generator for each parameter of the class's constructor for which there is a generator. The arguments are passed by the names of the parameters, so that the constructor uses the default value of a parameter for which there is no generator, also when there is one for a parameter after it.
Generates a value of one of the given generators. The first choice is the index of the generator, so the first generator is the simplest one.
Generates arrays with the given keys and a value of the respective generator for each of them.

Generates strings that a regular expression matches, from the nodes that it was parsed into. A string that the regular expression does not match, for instance because an anchor is neither at its start nor at its end, is rejected.
Generates valid UTF-8 strings. Their length is the number of characters (code points), not the number of bytes.
Generates lists that consist of one value of each of the given generators.
Generates URLs (RFC 3986) with an authority: a scheme, optional user information, a host, an optional port, a path, an optional query, and an optional fragment.
Generates UUIDs (RFC 9562) in their canonical form.
Factory for the generators that the parameters of properties are generated with.
Thrown when a generator is created or composed with invalid arguments.

Thrown when a generator cannot be created with the class or the method that it is specified with. The message is the reason, which the caller reports for the property or the state machine that specifies the generator.
Thrown when a property cannot be checked, for instance because no generator can be determined for one of its parameters.
Thrown when a state machine cannot be run, for instance because it has no rule or a pool from which one of its rules takes a value is not produced by any of them.
Thrown when a PHPDoc type cannot be parsed.
The numeric values that the examples of a property observed with TestCase::observe(), by their label, and their statistics.

A property after its metadata has been validated: the generator for each of its parameters that is derived from its type or where it comes from otherwise, its explicit examples, the minimum percentages of its examples that are required to be classified with labels, and the methods of its test case class that are registered with #[GeneratorFor].
Validates the metadata of a property before it is checked.

An example of a property: the arguments with which its test method is called, and what the example records while it runs, with assume(), draw(), runStateMachine(), classify(), observe(), and target() of TestCase, which delegate to it, and the throwable that ended it.

What the examples of a property that were generated and checked while the property was checked amount to: how many were checked and rejected, and why, how they were classified, what they observed, and the assertions that they performed. From these it decides whether further examples are generated and whether the property is considered risky, and why.
Alternatives of a regular expression, separated by |, of which the first is the simplest one.
A set of characters: of Unicode scalar values, which are encoded as UTF-8, for a regular expression with the u modifier, and of bytes otherwise.

One character of a set, for a character class, for an escape sequence such as \d, or for the dot. ASCII characters are generated more often than others, and the simplest character of the set comes first.
A literal string, which is generated without a choice. An assertion such as ^ or \b is the empty string.
A part of a regular expression from which strings are generated that the part matches.
Parses a regular expression, with its delimiters and modifiers, into the nodes from which strings are generated that the regular expression matches as a whole.
A part of a regular expression with a quantifier, which is repeated from its minimum to its maximum number of times, the minimum being the simplest.
Parts of a regular expression that follow one another.
The characters that an escape sequence such as \w, or a POSIX class such as [:alpha:], matches in a regular expression with the u modifier.

A parameter of a step of a state machine: it receives a value from a pool (#[FromPool]), or a value of a generator, which is the one that is specified with #[ForAll] or #[ForAllExternal], or the one that is derived from its type.

A state machine after its metadata has been validated: the methods that are called once before its steps are taken (#[InitializeStateMachine]), its rules (#[StateMachineRule]), and its invariants (#[StateMachineInvariant]), each in the order in which it is declared, with those that a parent class declares before those that the class that extends it declares.

Validates the metadata of a state machine before it is run, and creates the generators for the parameters of its steps that do not receive values from pools: the generators that are specified with #[ForAll] or #[ForAllExternal] and the generators that are derived from the types of the parameters with the deriver of the property that runs the state machine, which knows the generators that are registered for it with #[GeneratorFor].
Runs a state machine with the choices of an example of a property, so that its steps are generated, replayed, and shrunk together with the arguments of the property.

A step of a state machine: a method with #[StateMachineRule], which can be taken any number of times while its precondition holds, or a method with

[InitializeStateMachine], which is called once before the rules are taken.
An item of an array shape: a key, which may be optional, and the type of its value. The key of an item of a shape such as list{int, string} is null.
An array shape such as array{name: string, age?: int} or list{int, string}.

PHP discards doc comments when OPcache is active and opcache.save_comments is disabled. The doc comment of a method is then read from the source file that declares the method, so that the types in its @param tags are used regardless of the configuration of OPcache. Each file is parsed only once.
Splits a PHPDoc type into tokens. Tokens are read on demand, so that the text that follows a type, for instance the description of a @param tag, is not lexed.
An integer, floating-point, or string literal, for instance 42 or 'a'.

Determines the namespace and the imports that apply to the declaration of a class, an interface, a trait, or an enumeration, or to a statement outside of such a declaration, the way PHP resolves names. Each file is parsed only once.

Resolves the class names in the PHPDoc types of a method against the namespace and the imports of the file that declares the method, the same way PHPStan does. For a method that is declared in a trait, these are the namespace and the imports of the trait's file, while self and static refer to the class that uses the trait.
A keyword such as int or non-empty-string, or a class name, optionally with generic arguments, for instance list or int<0, max>. T[] is parsed as array.
A type written as ?T. T|null is parsed as UnionType.
The types of the parameters of a method as they are declared in its doc comment with the tags param, phpstan-param, and psalm-param.

Parses the source files from which the doc comments of methods and the namespaces and imports that apply to declarations are read. The nodes of the file that was parsed last are kept, so that a file whose doc comments and namespaces and imports are both needed, one after the other, is parsed once.
A type as it is written in PHPDoc, after it has been parsed. It is not interpreted: class names are not resolved, and whether a generator can be derived for the type is not known.
Parses the PHPDoc types that generators can be derived from:
Generates values of type T for the parameters of a property.
Thrown when an object of a class that implements ValueGenerator but was not created by PHPUnit is used as a generator.

Checks a property: runs its explicit examples and then its generated examples, each as a new instance of the test case class, shrinks the first counterexample that is generated, and replays the minimal counterexample.
Keeps track of the comparators and object exporters that a test registers so that they can be unregistered once the test has finished.
The data set that a data provider provided for a test method.
Creates the test doubles that a test case class requests, registers mock objects with the test that requested them, and emits the corresponding events.

Assembles the code that boots PHPUnit in a child process, shared by every kind of child process the test runner spawns: the per-test process of a test that requires process isolation, and the persistent worker process of a parallel run.

The mechanics shared by the two consumers of the serialized result envelope that a process-isolated child or a parallel worker writes back to the parent: the ChildProcessResultProcessor and the parallel ResultAggregator.

What a property is decided on, for one of its examples, besides the outcome of the example: whether the property is risky for the assertions that its examples performed or for their contribution to code coverage.
A test that is run while another test is running would start before the other test is finished. The events of both tests would then not be bracketed by the events that start and finish each test.
Decides whether a test is run in a separate process.

Decides whether a test is risky for a reason that concerns the test as a whole: for the assertions that it performed or for its contribution to code coverage. For a property, these are decided on all of its examples.

The generator that is specified for a parameter of a property with the

[ForAll] or #[ForAllExternal] attribute of the parameter.
The pool from which a parameter of a method of a state machine receives a value, which is specified with the #[FromPool] attribute of the parameter.
A method of a state machine that is called once before its steps are taken, which is specified with the #[InitializeStateMachine] attribute.
Attribute information is static within a single PHP process.

An invariant of a state machine, which is specified with the

[StateMachineInvariant] attribute.
A rule of a state machine, which is specified with the #[StateMachineRule] attribute.
The state a reordering stage needs in order to transform the tests of a single test suite: the test suite itself and the history of previous test runs.
Only errors and failures are considered defects; a test that was skipped or marked incomplete, or that triggered an issue, is not hoisted to the front.
Decides how much a test status weighs when tests are ordered "defects first".
An ordered list of reordering stages that is applied to the tests of every test suite.
A single, well-defined transform over the list of tests of one test suite.
Sorts tests by the time they took during the previous test run.
Sorts tests by the time their source files were last modified.
Sorts tests small before medium before large before unknown.
Hoists the tests that were defective during the previous test run towards the front, so that a defect is reached as fast as possible.
Reorders the tests of a test suite in such a way as to resolve as many dependencies as possible. The algorithm leaves the tests in their original order when it can.
An extension that is bootstrapped in the child processes that run tests as well as in the main process.
Bootstraps, in the child process of a test that runs in a separate process, the configured extensions that implement ChildProcessExtension.
Registers the subscribers of the extensions that are bootstrapped in a child process with the dispatcher that collects the events of the test that the child process runs.
What a child process offers an extension that is bootstrapped in it: the registration of subscribers that receive the events of the tests that the child process runs.
Bootstraps, in a parallel worker process, the configured extensions that implement ChildProcessExtension.
Collects the subscribers that the extensions bootstrapped in a parallel worker process register.

The value of the --filter CLI option, compiled to the regular expressions used to select tests.
The wire format with which the parent process sends commands to a worker on the worker's control channel, its standard input.
The outcome of a WorkUnit that a worker has finished: the serialized result envelope written by the worker, together with the unit it belongs to and the nonce that authenticates the envelope.

The descriptor of the suite that aggregates the tests of a data provider method. Its members are described recursively so that the suite travels to the worker as a suite and emits, inside the worker, the event envelope that nests its tests in the logger output.
The units of a chunk that have not been dispatched yet.

Keeps the events that units streamed before it is their turn in the release sequence, and what their workers wrote to their standard output and to their standard error before they streamed them, in a temporary file rather than in memory.
The wire format with which a worker streams events to the parent process while a unit of work is still running.
Records, inside a worker process, that a test method whose test is run more than once passed, so that the tests of the same unit that depend on it can run.

A worker process that boots PHPUnit once and then executes an arbitrary number of tests, each in response to a command received on its control channel (its standard input). A unit of work is a whole test class; the worker reconstructs it from the dispatched command, runs it, and reports the result back through the filesystem (see dispatch() and poll()).
Runs PHPT tests concurrently, each as its own child process, in the main PHPUnit process.

A unit of work for a single PHPT test, identified by the path of its .phpt file. A PHPT test is not a PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and carries no test data, so the worker reconstructs it from nothing more than this file path.
The number of units that may execute concurrently, shared by everything that runs units side by side in a parallel run.

The descriptor of the suite that checks a property. The suite travels to the worker as a suite so that the property is checked inside the worker: its examples are generated, run, and shrunk there, and only the events that the property is reported with travel back.

The descriptor of the suite that aggregates the repetitions of a repeated test method. All repetitions are described; the suite travels to the worker as a suite so that its failure threshold is applied inside the worker, which skips the remaining repetitions once the threshold is exceeded.
Collects the results that the workers produce and replays them into the parent process' event subsystem.

The descriptor of the suite that aggregates the attempts of a retried test method. Only the first attempt is described; the suite travels to the worker as a suite so that the additional attempts are built and run inside the worker, from the same descriptor.
Orders the units of a chunk for dispatch: the longest first.
The descriptor of a single test case: the test method to run, together with everything that distinguishes one invocation of that method from another.

A unit of work that bundles all of the selected tests of a single test class, kept together so that the class' shared fixtures (#[BeforeClass] /

[AfterClass]) and intra-class ordering are preserved when the unit is run by

a single worker.
One member of a test class work unit, in the form in which it travels to the worker process that runs the unit.
A unit of work distributed to a worker process.
Provides, inside a worker process, the data of the data-provided tests of the unit the worker is running.
A fixed-size pool of PersistentWorkers across which units of work are distributed.
The signal through which the caller that drives the generator returned by TestCase::execute() declares that it has abandoned the test.

Runs the examples of the properties of a test suite one at a time, for tools that drive property-based tests themselves, a fuzzer that is guided by code coverage, for instance.

Applies a ReorderPipeline to every test suite of a tree of test suites, depth first, so that the tests of a test suite are reordered before the test suite itself is reordered within its parent.
Thrown into the test that is running when the time limit for the test run is exceeded.

Derives the seed of a test run from the hash of the Git commit that is checked out in the working directory, so that test runs of the same commit, on a continuous integration server, for instance, use the same seed: the number that the first 15 hexadecimal digits of the hash make.

Prints the receipt of the test run as the last record of the compact output.
Runs a test suite by distributing its test classes across a pool of worker processes that execute them concurrently.

The lifecycle that every test runner performs around the execution of the test suite: seeding the randomizer, sorting and filtering the suite, and emitting the test runner events that bracket the execution.

Registers a subscriber with the direct dispatcher that events are dispatched to as they are collected, so that it receives the events of the test that a child process runs while the test is running. Registers a subscriber that is notified of events as they are diverted by a collection window, in addition to any subscriber that is notified when the window's owner forwards them.

Add the given events to the collection, as if they had been emitted through this emitter: this is how the events of a run that was diverted through a collection window become part of the collection after all.
Registers a subscriber that is notified of events as they are collected, in addition to any subscriber that is notified when they are forwarded.

Re-target this emitter to another dispatcher and telemetry system, as if it had been constructed with them. The events that are emitted from now on carry the telemetry of the last event whose telemetry was measured. Measuring the telemetry of an event takes most of the time that emitting it takes, and a process in which nothing reads the telemetry of events does not need it.
Registers subscribers that are notified of events while they are being collected instead of dispatched, for instance for an attempt of a retried test.

Mint an emitter that collects its events into an independent collection, without sealing this facade or replacing its emitter. The seed of the random number generator of the property, which is derived from the seed of the test run and the ID of the test.

Generates the values of $base and values that $extend builds from them, nested up to $maximumDepth levels. $extend receives a generator for the values of one level and returns a generator for the values of the next level, which contain them:

Generates objects of the given class the way they are generated for a parameter of a property whose type is the class: with the generator that the test case class registers for it with #[GeneratorFor], as points in time or the cases of an enumeration, or with new, using arguments that are generated for the parameters of the constructor.

Generates values the way they are generated for a parameter of a property whose type, in its @param tag, is $type. Class names in the type are resolved against the namespace and the imports that apply where fromType() is called.

Generates UUIDs (RFC 9562) of the versions in $versions, in their canonical form: lowercase hexadecimal digits in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4, and 12. The version and the variant (RFC 9562) are set, the other bits are biased towards all zeros and all ones in each field. The timestamp of versions 1, 6, and 7 is one field, which is laid out as the version requires, so that it shrinks towards the epoch of the version. The bits of the other versions are not derived from anything: a UUID of version 3 or 5 is not the hash of a name, for instance.
Generates IPv4 addresses of $network, given in CIDR notation, in dotted decimal notation without leading zeros.

Generates IPv6 addresses of $network, given in CIDR notation, in their canonical text representation (RFC 5952): lowercase hexadecimal digits without leading zeros, the first longest run of at least two groups of zeros compressed to "::", and the last 32 bits of an IPv4-mapped address in dotted decimal notation. No zone identifier is generated.
Generates domain names of at most $maximumLength characters, which consist of letters, digits, and hyphens (RFC 1123), in lowercase and without a trailing dot.
Generates email addresses (RFC 5321) of at most 254 characters, with a local part of at most 64 characters and a domain name from domainNames().

Generates URLs (RFC 3986) of the schemes in $schemes with an authority: a scheme, a host, an optional port, a path, an optional query, and an optional fragment. With $userInformation, some URLs have user information, a user name and an optional password, in front of the host.

Generates points in time from $minimum to $maximum as DateTimeImmutable objects in one of the time zones in $timezones, which are given as their identifier, their abbreviation, or their offset from UTC. By default, the points in time are from 0001-01-01 00:00:00 UTC to 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC, in UTC, and without microseconds.

Generates the identifiers of time zones, such as Europe/Berlin. Half of them are from time zones whose offsets or transitions between standard time and daylight saving time are notable, such as Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+05:45), Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14:00), Australia/Lord_Howe (daylight saving time of 30 minutes), Europe/Dublin (negative daylight saving time), or Pacific/Apia (which skipped a day), the other half are from all time zones that DateTimeZone::listIdentifiers() lists.
The public static method that describes a counterexample of the property, null when none is specified.
Runs the state machine, and observes the number of steps that it takes, and the number of steps that it takes with each rule.

Whether the example was discarded because assume() was called with false, or because draw() or runStateMachine() could not generate a value. An example that failed or errored afterwards, in tearDown() or in the destructor of a test double, for instance, was not discarded.
Why the example was rejected, when it was.
The labels with which the example was classified by classify().
The numeric values that the example observed with observe(), with their labels, in the order in which they were observed.
The scores that the example targeted with target(), by their label.
The number of steps that the state machine that the example ran with runStateMachine() took, null when it did not run one or the state machine did not finish.
The throwable that ended the example: the one that caused its failure or error, as it was raised, or the TimeoutException when the example exceeded its time limit.
Whether the property was checked for as many generated examples as it is to be checked for.
Whether the property was checked for at least half of the generated examples for which it is to be checked.

Whether no further examples are generated because too many examples were rejected before enough examples were checked. The reason for which examples were rejected whose advice is given is remembered for the message with which the property is considered risky.

Records the assertions that an example that was checked performed, and whether it contributed to code coverage. This is recorded for an example that is not counted as one of the examples for which the property was checked, because it was skipped, for instance, as well.
The messages with which the property is considered risky.

The surrogates that a range of Unicode scalar values spans, from a character below them to a character above them, for instance, are not part of the set, as they are not characters and cannot be encoded.
All characters: the Unicode scalar values, that is, all code points except the surrogates, or all bytes.
The ASCII characters.
The characters of $within that are not in this set.
Returns the member with the given index in the order from the simplest to the least simple character, encoded as UTF-8 or as a byte.
The pool from which the parameter receives a value, null when it receives a generated value.
Whether the value that the parameter receives is removed from its pool.
The generator of the values that the parameter receives, null when it receives a value from a pool.
The steps that were taken, written as PHP code, in the order in which they were taken, with the invariant that failed, if one did. They are only recorded with an exporter.

The steps that were taken, as steps() returns them, followed by the step that is being taken or the invariant that is being checked, for the report of the example that was run when the PHP process ended. The steps that were taken without an exporter are written as PHP code with the given one: their arguments are exported in the state in which the steps left them, and the values that they returned are not written.
The number of steps that were taken, not counting the initializations and the rules that were skipped.
The number of steps that were taken with each rule, in the order in which the rules are declared.
Returns the doc comment of the method, which is read from the source file that declares the method when PHP has discarded it, or false when the method does not have one.

Returns the doc comments of the promoted parameters of the constructor that have one, by the names of the parameters. They are read from the source file that declares the constructor when PHP has discarded them, where only a doc comment that precedes the parameter, its attributes and modifiers included, is found.
Returns the doc comment of the method as it is written in the source file that declares it, or null when the method has none there or the file cannot be read or parsed.
Returns the doc comments of the promoted parameters of the constructor as they are written in the source file that declares it, by the names of the parameters.

Returns the name context that applies to the declaration of the class (or interface, trait, or enumeration) that contains the given line, or to the statement outside of such a declaration that contains it, such as the declaration of a function, or the context of the global namespace without imports when the file cannot be read or parsed or no declaration or statement contains the line.
Resolves the class names in a PHPDoc type that is written at the given line of the given file, for instance as the argument of a call, where self and static refer to the given class.
Resolves a class name as it is written in a PHPDoc type, possibly with a leading backslash, to a fully qualified class name without a leading backslash.

Returns the shortest name under which the class can be referred to in the file that declares the method: its alias or its namespace-relative name when there is one, and its fully qualified name with a leading backslash otherwise.
Returns these types together with the types that the doc comments of promoted constructor parameters declare with a @var tag, a @phpstan-var tag, or a @psalm-var tag.
The tag that declares the type of the parameter: var for the @var tag, the @phpstan-var tag, or the @psalm-var tag of a promoted constructor parameter, param otherwise.
Returns the nodes of the file, or null when the file cannot be read or parsed.
The value of a literal, the name of an identifier or variable, or the symbol.
Parses the type that the lexer is positioned at and leaves the lexer positioned at the token that follows the type.
Returns a generator for the values that $mapper returns for the values of this generator.
Returns a generator for the values of this generator that satisfy $predicate. Values that do not satisfy it are generated again. When this fails too often, the example is rejected.
Returns a generator for the values of the generators that $mapper returns for the values of this generator.
The number of examples for which the property is to be checked.
The test run history from which the counterexamples that were remembered when the property was last falsified are taken.

The choice sequences of the counterexamples that were remembered when the property was last falsified, for a process that has no test run history to take them from: a worker process of a parallel test run, to which they travel with the description of the property.
The choice sequences of the counterexamples that were remembered when the property was last falsified, one for each way in which it was falsified, and an empty list when none are remembered.

Runs one example of the property, with its full lifecycle, on its own rather than while the property is checked, with arguments that are generated from the given choices. The example is neither shrunk nor reported, and the events that are emitted while it runs are not dispatched.
Runs one example of the property, as replayExample() does, with arguments that are generated from choices that are drawn from a random number generator that is seeded with the given seed.

Discards the generators of the examples that are run on their own, so that they are created again for the next one. They are discarded when the test class is finished, as they can depend on what the hook methods that are called before its first test set up, setUpBeforeClass(), for instance, which are called again when the test class is prepared again.
Returns a string representation of the object.

Applies to a test case the configuration that build() derives from the metadata of the test method and from the configuration of the test runner: process isolation, the preservation of global state, and the backup of global variables and static properties.
This method is called before the first test of this test class is run.
This method is called after the last test of this test class is run.
This method is called before each test.
Performs assertions shared by all tests of a test case.
Performs assertions shared by all tests of a test case.
This method is called after each test.
Returns a string representation of the test case.

Makes this test an example of a property: the test method is called with the arguments of the example instead of the data of a data provider and the return values of dependencies. The identity of the test does not change, and an example is neither registered as passed nor run in a separate process.
The example of a property that this test is, null when it is not one.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is never executed.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is executed at least N times.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is executed at least once.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is executed exactly once.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is executed exactly $count times.
Returns a matcher that matches when the method is executed at most N times.
Suspends the buffering of the test's output so that it can be resumed in another output buffering context, for instance inside a coroutine started by an implementation of invokeTestMethod().
Resumes the buffering of the test's output that was suspended using suspendOutputBuffering().
Discards the current example of a property when $condition is false. A discarded example neither passes nor fails, and it does not count towards the number of examples that are checked.

Draws a value from a generator in the body of a property, for instance a value that depends on the arguments of the property or on values that were drawn before. The values that are drawn are replayed and shrunk together with the arguments of the property, and the values that the minimal counterexample draws are reported, described by their labels.

Runs a state machine in the body of a property: an object whose methods with #[StateMachineRule] are the steps that can be taken, whose methods with #[InitializeStateMachine] are called before the first step, and whose methods with #[StateMachineInvariant] are called after each step, or only after the last one with #[StateMachineInvariant(atEnd: true)].

Classifies the current example of a property with the given label, so that the statistics of the property state how many of its examples were classified with it, and #[RequireClassification] can require a minimum percentage of them. An example can be classified with several labels.

Observes a numeric value of the current example of a property, for instance the size of a generated list, so that the statistics of the property state how many values were observed with the label, and their minimum, median, mean, 90th percentile, and maximum. An example can observe more than one value with the same label.

Targets a score for the current example of a property: once half of the examples of the property have been checked, the other half are spent on searching for examples with higher scores, by changing the choices of the example with the highest score so far. A property that fails only for rare examples is falsified more often when a score measures how close an example comes to them. The highest score of each label is stated in the statistics of the property.
Sets up an expectation for an exception to be raised by the code under test.
Returns a builder object to create mock objects using a fluent interface.
Creates a mock object for the specified interface or class.
Creates a journal that the invocations of methods of mock objects can be recorded in, in the order in which they happen.
Creates (and configures) a mock object for the specified interface or class.
Creates a partial mock object for the specified interface or class.
This method is called when a test method did not execute successfully.
Returns a builder object to create test stubs using a fluent interface.
Creates a test stub for the specified interface or class.
Creates (and configures) a test stub for the specified interface or class.
Returns true when the test can be run.
Backs up and then sets the environment variables that are configured using #[WithEnvironmentVariable] for the given test method.
An expectation failure raised by an invocation count rule while the test method was running counts as an assertion.
The head of a child process template: rendered with the INI settings the child is to apply — an empty string when there are none.

The given value as the contents of a single-quoted string literal of a template: the value is exported as a string literal of its own that is concatenated with the empty strings that the quotes of the template delimit.
Verify the nonce that prefixes the serialized result and strip it, returning the bare payload.

Decode a verified serialized result envelope into the shape that every consumer requires: an object that carries a collection of events and the tests that passed. Null is returned when the payload does not decode to that shape; each consumer reports that in its own way. A consumer that requires more of the envelope — the per-test result fields that only the process-isolation envelope carries — validates those on top.
Merge the code coverage carried by a decoded result envelope into the parent's coverage, when coverage collection is active and the envelope actually carries it.

Whether the example executed code for which code coverage is collected, null when this was not checked because contribution to code coverage is not required or no code coverage was collected for the example.

A test is run in a separate process when the test or the configuration requests it, unless the test already runs in isolation (it then is the test in the separate process) or its requirements are not satisfied (it then is skipped, which does not warrant a separate process).
A test requests to be run in a separate process, or the configuration requests this for all tests.
Returns why a test that performed no assertions is risky, or null when it performed assertions, is not expected to perform any, or useless tests are not reported.
Returns why a test that is not expected to perform assertions is risky because it performed some, or null when it is not.
Returns why a test that did not contribute to code coverage is risky, or null when it did or when this was not checked.
Whether PHPUnit's error handler handles the issues that are triggered by the test, which it does unless #[WithoutErrorHandler] is used.

A time limit cannot be enforced without the pcntl extension, and it is not enforced while a debugger is active, whether it is the configured time limit or the one of an example of a property that is passed.
The message that is printed when the PHP process ends while the test is run.
Runs an example of a property, in the process that runs the property.

Creates an empty test suite for the given test class, to which tests of that class are then added one by one. Used where the tests of the class have already been selected, as for a work unit of a parallel test run, rather than found by reflecting on the class.
Adds a test to the suite.
Adds the tests from the given class to the suite.
Wraps both addTest() and addTestSuite as well as the separate import statements for the user's convenience.
Counts the number of test cases that will be run by this test.

The identifiers of the tests are only determined when they are asked for, which is only the case when tests are filtered by group. A test that is run builds the event value object that provides its identifier anyway, and caches it, so determining the identifiers eagerly only adds work for tests that are never run.

The repetitions of a repeated test and the attempts of a retried test are aggregated by an IterativeTestSuite whose runTests() method implements the repetition and retry logic. Running the test cases returned by this method individually bypasses this logic: an IterativeTestSuite must be treated as an atomic unit.
Returns the tests aggregated by this test suite: all of them, and not only those that the test selection has selected.
Set tests of the test suite.

Remove the tests from the test suite without running them, for a caller that runs them in a different way (see ParallelTestRunner). Like run(), which takes the tests out of the test suite before it runs them, this lets each test object be destructed as soon as it has run and its caller has let go of it (see #5875).
Calls the hook methods of the test class that are called before its first test, when the examples of its properties are run one at a time outside of a test run rather than when its tests are run.
Calls the hook methods of the test class that are called after its last test, when the examples of its properties are run one at a time outside of a test run, after the last of these examples.
The emitter with which the test suite was created.
Runs the tests aggregated by this test suite.
The first part of the receipt of the test run is written, and flushed, before this method returns, so that the logfile of a test run that dies says what was run.
Writes the second part of the receipt of the test run, which is the last content of the logfile: its presence shows that the test run reached its end.

A test class that is skipped as a whole is reported as a skipped test suite, and its tests never start: none of them emits the event that ends a test, which is what every other test is recorded on. They are recorded here so that they are not missing from the output, which would otherwise show fewer tests than the test run counted.

The metadata that backs --covers, --uses and --requires-php-extension is mapped to a group of its own so that these options can be implemented as a selection by group. Everything that selects tests this way has to name these groups the same way, which is why they are only named here.

The class on which the method that returns the generator is called: the test case class, unless the generator is specified with

[ForAllExternal].
The name of a public static method of the class that is returned by className() that returns the generator, or a static closure that returns it.
Whether the value is removed from the pool.
The name of the pool to which the value that the method returns is added, null when it is not added to a pool.
The number of examples to check, or null for the configured default.
Whether the invariant is only checked after the initialization and after the last step rather than after every step.
The name of the method of the state machine that tells whether the rule can be taken, null when it can always be taken.
The name of the pool to which the value that the rule returns is added, null when it is not added to a pool.

A code coverage object that holds only the code coverage data that has been collected and the tests it was collected for: what the main process merges into the code coverage that it collects when a parallel worker process ships the code coverage of a unit it ran.
Stops collecting code coverage data for the current test, an example of a property that passed without performing assertions, and holds the data back instead of appending it, see appendHeldBack().

Appends the code coverage data that was held back for the examples of a property, and returns whether it contributed to code coverage, or null when that is not checked because contribution to code coverage is not required or no data was appended.
Discards the code coverage data that was held back for the examples of a property, like the data of a test that is considered risky because it did not perform any assertions.

The deprecation is not added to the filtered deprecations, which count towards stopping the test run. A deprecation of collected events is added to them when, and only if, the collected events are forwarded, which notifies this collector through testTriggeredDeprecation().

Prepares the collector for a process that runs tests in isolation from the main process and forwards their events to it: the child process of a test that runs in process isolation, or a worker process of a parallel test run.
Return true to ignore the deprecation, false to let PHPUnit process it.

Handles the issues that are triggered until disable() is called as issues of the given test, which is not on the call stack meanwhile: the issues that are triggered while the arguments for the examples of a property are generated, for instance, are issues of the property, and an example of a property, which is run by the test runner rather than by TestCase::run(), is not on the call stack while code coverage data is collected for it.

Reports the issues that were triggered in the test case context of a property, while the test suite was built, for instance, once for the property rather than for each of its examples. The error handler must be enabled for the property with enableForTestNotOnCallStack().
A weight greater than zero hoists the test towards the front of the test suite; tests of equal weight keep their relative order.
The names of the stages of this pipeline, in the order in which they are applied.
How this stage is named in diagnostics.
Shuts down the extensions that were bootstrapped successfully, in the order in which they were bootstrapped. An extension whose shutdown fails does not keep the others from being shut down.
Capabilities of a test run that does not bootstrap any extension.
Register a subscriber that is notified only of the events that were emitted in this process.

Shut down the extensions that were bootstrapped successfully, in the order in which they were bootstrapped. An extension whose shutdown fails does not keep the others from being shut down; the failure is returned as a warning, which the worker reports to the main process.
Whether the name of a group is parsed as a conjunction of the names of other groups instead of as the name of that group.
Whether a group is named by this selection, and knowing which tests are in it is therefore worth the effort.
The regular expression to match against the name of a test, including the name of its data set.
The regular expression to match against the name of a test method, not including the name of a data set.
Garbage that the tests whose events are collected rather than dispatched leave behind is collected as well. The event that reports this is collected with the events of the test.
Return null to defer to the next resolver in the chain.
Encode one command for transport on the control channel. The newline that delimits it from the next command is not part of the result.
Decode one command received on the control channel.
The name of a data provider test suite is the name of its test class and the name of its test method, separated by "::" (see TestBuilder).
Take the next unit to dispatch.
Drop the units that have not been dispatched yet; the queue is empty afterwards.
The collections of events that were added for the unit, each with the output and the error output that were added with it, in the order in which they were added.

Encode one frame: the given events, serialized and prefixed with the nonce that authenticates them, with the numbers of bytes that the worker has written to its standard output and to its standard error so far, and with the length of the whole payload.

Decode the complete frames at the beginning of $data into the collections of events they carry, each with the numbers of bytes that the worker had written to its standard output and to its standard error when it wrote the frame.

Boot a fresh worker process in place of one that has died. The new process keeps the worker's ordinal identity (PHPUNIT_WORKER_ID), so that resources partitioned per worker stay partitioned, but receives a new PHPUNIT_WORKER_TOKEN, so that it cannot collide with resources that the dead process left behind.
Send a unit of work to the worker without waiting for it to finish.
Whether the worker is currently executing a dispatched unit.
The unit the worker is currently executing; null when it is idle. The pool derives from this which of the units in flight is the one the ordered output is waiting for (see WorkerPool).
Whether the worker process is still usable. A worker that died while running a unit is no longer usable and must not be dispatched to again.
Check, without blocking, whether the dispatched unit has finished and, if so, harvest its result; if the worker has died without finishing it, report the unit as crashed instead.

Ask the worker process to halt the unit it is executing, because the results collected so far call for the test runner to stop (--stop-on-*): the worker process lets the test that is running finish, starts no further test, and runs the methods that run after the last test of the class, as the sequential test runner does when it stops (see worker.tpl). The request is made through a file, as the commands are, and the worker process then reports completion as usual.

Terminate the worker process immediately, abandoning the unit it is executing: the unit's result is neither awaited nor harvested. Used when the deadline of a time limit for the test run has passed, also while the test runner waits for a unit that it asked to halt.

Terminate the worker process while it is executing a unit that has to be abandoned because the time limit for the test run has been exceeded, and return that unit. The events that the worker has streamed since the previous poll are handed to the given callback first, so that the tests that finished before the worker was terminated are reported.

Stop the worker process gracefully: the worker shuts down the extensions that were bootstrapped in it and exits. The warnings that a failed bootstrap or a failed shutdown of an extension produced are reported through a result file, whose content is trusted only when it carries the nonce of the stop command, and are returned: every worker process bootstraps the same extensions, so the caller reports each warning once rather than once per worker process (see WorkerPool).
Run the given PHPT units to completion, invoking the callback once for each unit as it finishes (in completion order, not suite order) with its suite index and the events it collected.
Accept the units to run without running them yet: the caller is expected to drive the runner with tick() until isFinished() reports completion.

Advance the runner by one polling round: start every queued unit that a free slot and its conflict keys allow, and harvest the children that have finished. Returns whether the round made progress; a caller driving the runner in a loop is expected to sleep briefly when it did not, so that polling does not spin the CPU.
Whether every unit accepted by begin() has finished.
Whether any test is currently running.

Whether the test that is currently running conflicts with "all" and must therefore run entirely on its own. While this reports true, the caller must not start any other work — the worker pool must not dispatch units — or the promised exclusivity would be broken.

Abandon the run, because the results collected so far call for the test runner to stop (--stop-on-*): the tests that have not been started yet are dropped, and the running tests are asked to halt. A halted test finishes the section that is running and then runs only what must still run — the --CLEAN-- section, when the --FILE-- section has run — and skips everything else, the remaining repetitions or attempts of a repeated or retried test included (see Interruption), so that the test does not leave its fixtures behind.

Abandon the run without waiting for the sections that are running: the tests that have not been started yet are dropped, and the child processes of the running tests are terminated. Used when the deadline of a time limit for the test run passes while the test runner waits for the tests that it asked to halt.
How often the test is run in a row, each run reported on its own; more than once when --repeat was used.
The repetitions of a repeated test that are to be run: all of them, unless test selection, such as with --run-test-id, picked only some.
How often the test may be attempted before a failure is reported as its result; more than once when --retry was used.

The conflict keys declared by the test's --CONFLICTS-- section. While a test that conflicts with key K is running, no other test that conflicts with K may run. The reserved key "all" conflicts with every other test, so a test that declares it runs on its own.

The estimated duration of this unit's tests, in seconds: what a previous run recorded for them, and for the tests that have not run before what the size they declare promises (see TestClassWorkUnit); 0.0 when neither is available. The scheduler dispatches the units of a chunk longest first (see Scheduler).
Take one slot, when one is available. A caller that acquired a slot must release() it once the unit it started has finished.
Whether a slot is available right now, so that a caller can find out without taking one whether it is worth looking for a unit to start.
How many slots are available right now.

Register a unit that is to be run, in the main process, at the point its suite index comes up in the release sequence: the release sequence stops at its index, and the runner runs it through runPendingUnit().
Register the events that a unit which has already run in the main process — a PHPT test, run by the PHPT runner — collected, to be forwarded when the unit's turn in the release sequence comes.

Whether the release sequence has stopped at the index of a unit that is to be run in the main process: everything that precedes the unit in suite order has been forwarded, and the unit waits to be run through runPendingUnit().
Whether the unit that the release sequence has stopped at must run alone: it is run through runPendingUnit() only once nothing else is executing.

Run the unit that the release sequence has stopped at, then resume releasing. The caller is responsible for calling this for an exclusive unit only once nothing else is executing — that is what makes the unit's execution exclusive.
Accept a finished worker unit and release every unit that has now become releasable in suite order.
Accept events that a worker streamed while its unit is still running.

Whether the unit at the given index may be re-run from scratch: true when none of its streamed events have been forwarded yet. The events that were buffered for it are discarded, so that the events of the new attempt take their place. The worker pool makes this call before it retries a crashed unit on a fresh worker, because the retry re-runs all of the unit's tests and must not repeat any that were already reported.

Release every unit that is releasable in suite order, up to the next unit that is to be run in the main process. Called by the runner once the PHPT runner has handed over the events of a PHPT test, which are then forwarded as their turn comes.

Close the test suite envelopes that the forwarded events of the units that are still executing left open. Called when the run stops early and those units are halted: their remaining events, which would have closed the envelopes, are discarded, and the consumers that reconstruct the suite hierarchy from paired Started/Finished events need a balanced stream.

The estimated duration of this unit's tests, in seconds: what a previous run recorded for them, and for the tests that have not run before what the size they declare promises (see TestClassWorkUnit); 0.0 when neither is available. The scheduler dispatches the units of a chunk longest first (see Scheduler).
Describe one member of a work unit. Runs in the parent process.
Rebuild the member that this descriptor describes. Runs inside the worker process, which provides the data of the data-provided test cases among the members through the given data provider.
The name of the test method whose test, or tests, the described member consists of.

Rebuild the member that this descriptor describes and prepare it the way TestSuite::addTestMethod() prepares a member of the suite of a test class: with the dependencies of its test method. Runs inside the worker process.

The estimated duration of this unit's tests, in seconds: what a previous run recorded for them, and for the tests that have not run before what the size they declare promises (see TestClassWorkUnit); 0.0 when neither is available. The scheduler dispatches the units of a chunk longest first (see Scheduler).
The data set of the given name that the data provider of the given test method provides.
Run all of the given units across the pool, invoking the completion callback once for each unit as it finishes (in completion order, not suite order).

Accept the units to run without running them yet: the caller is expected to drive the pool with tick() until isFinished() reports completion. This is what lets the parallel test runner advance the worker pool and the PHPT runner side by side in one polling loop.

Advance the pool by one polling round: top the idle workers up with queued units, drain the events the busy workers have streamed, and harvest every worker that has finished its unit. Returns whether the round made progress; a caller driving the pool in a loop is expected to sleep briefly when it did not, so that polling does not spin the CPU.

Abandon the units that are queued and the units that are executing, because the time limit for the test run has been exceeded: the queued units are dropped, as halt() drops them, and the executing units are terminated and handed to the completion callback as aborted, so that the test that each of them was running is reported as aborted with the given message, as the sequential test runner reports the test that it aborts.

Abandon the run, because the results collected so far call for the test runner to stop (--stop-on-*): the units that have not been dispatched yet are dropped, and every worker that is busy executing a unit is asked to halt it as the sequential test runner stops — the test that is running finishes, no further test of the unit is started, and the methods that run after the last test of the class, such as tearDownAfterClass(), are run, so that the unit does not leave its fixtures behind.

Abandon the run without waiting for the units that are executing: the units that have not been dispatched yet are dropped, and every worker that is busy executing a unit is terminated without waiting for its result. Used when the deadline of a time limit for the test run passes while the test runner waits for the units that it asked to halt, and when the pool is stopped while units are executing; the workers that are idle stay alive and are shut down by stop() as usual.

A copy of the recorded passes without the values that the passed tests returned.
